topics.title: Meaning of Prehistory and History
topics.description: Distinction between prehistory (before writing) and history (recorded human past).

topics.title: The Discipline of History
topics.description: Importance of history, primary vs secondary sources, dating techniques (radiocarbon, potassium-argon), periodization, and Ethiopian historiography.

topics.title: The Evolution of Human Beings
topics.description: Scientific theory of evolution, hominid fossil discoveries in the Ethiopian Rift Valley (Ardipithecus kadabba/ramidus, Australopithecus afarensis Lucy/Dinknesh, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo sapiens Idaltu).

topics.title: The Stone Age
topics.description: Paleolithic (Oldowan, Acheulean tools), Mesolithic, and Neolithic Revolution (domestication of plants like teff/enset and animals).

topics.title: The Emergence of States
topics.description: Theories of state formation: agriculture surplus, irrigation management, trade, religion, and military leadership.

book_chapters.title: Unit 1: The Discipline of History and Human Evolution

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 2: Ancient World Civilizations up to c. 500 AD
book_chapters.description: 2.1 Ancient Civilizations of Africa; 2.2 Civilizations in Asia; 2.3 Ancient Civilization of Latin America; 2.4 Civilizations in Europe; 2.5 Rise and Spread of Christianity

topics.title: Ancient Civilizations of Africa
topics.description: Ancient Egypt (Nile gift, pharaohs, pyramids, hieroglyphics, mummification) and Kingdom of Kush/Meroe (iron smelting, Meroitic script).

topics.title: Civilizations in Asia
topics.description: Mesopotamia (Sumerians, cuneiform, Code of Hammurabi), Persia, Ancient India (Indus Valley, Hinduism, Buddhism), and Ancient China (Shang, Zhou, Qin, Han, Great Wall, silk, paper).

topics.title: Ancient Civilization of Latin America
topics.description: Maya, Inca, and Aztec civilizations: astronomical calendars, terraced agriculture, and monumental architecture.

topics.title: Civilizations in Europe
topics.description: Ancient Greece (Athens direct democracy, Sparta, philosophy, Olympics) and Ancient Rome (Roman Republic, Roman Empire, Roman law, engineering).

topics.title: Rise and Spread of Christianity
topics.description: Origins in 1st-century Judea, teachings of Jesus Christ, Roman persecution, Emperor Constantine (Edict of Milan 313 AD), and Council of Nicaea.

book_chapters.title: Unit 2: Ancient World Civilizations up to c. 500 AD

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 3: Peoples and States in Ethiopia and the Horn to the End of 13th C.
book_chapters.description: 3.1 Languages, Religions and Peoples of Ethiopia and the Horn; 3.2 Pre-Aksumite States and Their Geographical Setting; 3.3 The Aksumite Kingdom; 3.4 The Zagwe Dynasty; 3.5 The Sultanate of Shewa

topics.title: Languages, Religions and Peoples of Ethiopia and the Horn
topics.description: Afro-Asiatic (Cushitic, Semitic, Omotic) and Nilo-Saharan superfamilies; indigenous religions (Waaqeffanna), Judaism, Christianity (Ezana, Nine Saints), and Islam (First Hijra to Aksum in 615 AD).

topics.title: Pre-Aksumite States and Their Geographical Setting
topics.description: Land of Punt (myrrh, gold, ivory trade with Egypt) and Damat (D'mt, Yeha temple, Mukarib title, South Arabian contacts).

topics.title: The Aksumite Kingdom
topics.description: Rise of Aksum, Red Sea international trade at Adulis, coinage (gold, silver, bronze), monolithic stelae, territorial expansion, and causes of decline.

topics.title: The Zagwe Dynasty
topics.description: Mara Teklehaimanot, capital at Roha (Adafa), King Lalibela and the eleven rock-hewn monolithic churches, architectural legacy, and end of Zagwe rule (1270).

topics.title: The Sultanate of Shewa
topics.description: Makhzumite dynasty (founded c. 896 AD), trade routes linking the interior highlands with Zeila, and absorption by the Sultanate of Ifat.

book_chapters.title: Unit 3: Peoples and States in Ethiopia and the Horn to the End of 13th C.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 4: The Middle Ages and Early Modern World, c. 500 to 1750s
book_chapters.description: 4.1 The Middle Ages in Europe; 4.2 The Middle Ages in Asia; 4.3 Development of Early Capitalism; 4.4 The Age of Explorations and Discoveries; 4.5 The Renaissance; 4.6 The Reformation; 4.7 Industrial Revolution

topics.title: The Middle Ages in Europe
topics.description: Western European feudalism (lords, vassals, serfs, manorial system), the Catholic Church, the Byzantine Empire (Justinian Code, Constantinople), and the Crusades.

topics.title: The Middle Ages in Asia
topics.description: Rise and expansion of Islam (Prophet Muhammad, Hijra 622 AD, Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates, Islamic golden age science), Ottoman Empire, and Ming/Tang/Song China.

topics.title: Development of Early Capitalism
topics.description: Growth of medieval towns, merchant and craft guilds, banking (Medici), joint-stock companies, and mercantilism.

topics.title: The Age of Explorations and Discoveries
topics.description: Portuguese and Spanish maritime voyages: Henry the Navigator, Vasco da Gama, Christopher Columbus, Ferdinand Magellan, and global trade shifts.

topics.title: The Renaissance
topics.description: Italian and Northern European Rebirth: humanism, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Shakespeare, Gutenberg printing press, and scientific inquiry (Copernicus, Galileo).

topics.title: The Reformation
topics.description: Martin Luther (95 Theses, 1517), John Calvin, Protestant churches, English Reformation, and the Catholic Counter-Reformation (Council of Trent, Jesuits).

topics.title: Industrial Revolution
topics.description: Origins of the Industrial Revolution in 18th-century Britain: textile mechanization, James Watt's steam engine, coal and iron.

book_chapters.title: Unit 4: The Middle Ages and Early Modern World, c. 500 to 1750s

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 5: Peoples and States of Africa to 1500
book_chapters.description: 5.1 Languages and Peoples of Africa; 5.2 States in North Africa; 5.3 Spread of Islam in West Africa; 5.4 States in Western Africa; 5.5 Equatorial, Central and Eastern Africa; 5.6 Southern Africa; 5.7 Intra and Inter-Continental Relations

topics.title: Languages and Peoples of Africa
topics.description: The four major African language superfamilies: Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo (including Bantu migrations), Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan.

topics.title: States in North Africa
topics.description: Fatimid Caliphate in Egypt, Almoravid and Almohad Amazigh (Berber) empires in the Maghreb, and Mamluk rule.

topics.title: Spread of Islam in West Africa
topics.description: Peaceful diffusion of Islam across the Sahara via Amazigh merchants, growth of Islamic scholarship in Timbuktu, Gao, and Kano.

topics.title: States in Western Africa
topics.description: Ancient Ghana (Wagadu), Empire of Mali (Sundiata Keita, Mansa Musa), Songhai Empire (Sunni Ali, Askia Muhammad), Kanem-Bornu, and Hausa city-states.

topics.title: Equatorial, Central and Eastern Africa
topics.description: Kingdom of Kongo, Swahili coastal city-states (Kilwa, Mombasa, Zanzibar, Mogadishu), and Indian Ocean trade.

topics.title: Southern Africa
topics.description: Great Zimbabwe (stone enclosures, gold trade with Sofala), Mutapa (Mwene Mutapa) Empire, and Khoisan/Bantu societies.

topics.title: Intra and Inter-Continental Relations
topics.description: Trans-Saharan gold-salt caravan trade routes and Red Sea / Indian Ocean commercial networks.

book_chapters.title: Unit 5: Peoples and States of Africa to 1500

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 6: Africa and the Outside World 1500–1880s
book_chapters.description: 6.1 Contact with the Outside World; 6.2 Slavery and the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade; 6.3 The "Legitimate" Trade; 6.4 The White Settlement in South Africa; 6.5 European Explorers and Missionaries

topics.title: Contact with the Outside World
topics.description: Portuguese coastal forts (Elmina, Mombasa), Ottoman presence in North Africa, and shifting trade patterns.

topics.title: Slavery and the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
topics.description: Triangular Trade between Europe, West Africa, and the Americas; the Middle Passage; demographic, economic, and political devastation in Africa.

topics.title: The "Legitimate" Trade
topics.description: Abolition of the slave trade in the 19th century and transition to exporting palm oil, groundnuts, ivory, gum arabic, and cloves.

topics.title: The White Settlement in South Africa
topics.description: Dutch East India Company settlement at the Cape (1652), Boers/Afrikaners, Khoikhoi and Xhosa wars, British takeover, the Great Trek, and Zulu resistance under Shaka.

topics.title: European Explorers and Missionaries
topics.description: 19th-century European exploration of African rivers (Mungo Park, David Livingstone, Henry Morton Stanley) and missionary activities as precursors to colonization.

book_chapters.title: Unit 6: Africa and the Outside World 1500–1880s

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 7: States, Principalities, Population Movements & Interactions in Ethiopia 13th to Mid-16th C.
book_chapters.description: 7.1 The "Solomonic" Dynasty & the Christian Kingdom, 13th–16th C.; 7.2 The Muslim Principalities; 7.3 Relationship Between the Christian Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal, 1520s–1559; 7.4 Political and Socio-Economic Conditions of Southern and Central States in Ethiopia; 7.5 Population Movements, Expansion and Integration in Ethiopia; 7.6 Gadaa System of the Oromo; 7.7 Moggasa and Guddifacha & Egalitarian Systems of Governance

topics.title: The "Solomonic" Dynasty & the Christian Kingdom, 13th–16th C.
topics.description: Yekuno Amlak (1270), Kibre Negest ideology, roving royal capitals, Amba Gishen royal prison, territorial expansion under Amde Tsiyon and Zara Yaqob.

topics.title: The Muslim Principalities
topics.description: Zeila trade route and rise of Muslim sultanates: Ifat (Walasma dynasty), Hadiya, Fatagar, Dawaro, Bali, Mora, Adal.

topics.title: Relationship Between the Christian Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal, 1520s–1559
topics.description: Rivalry over control of the Zeila trade route, Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (Ahmad Gragn), Battle of Shimbra Kure (1529), Portuguese and Ottoman intervention, Battle of Woina Dega (1543).

topics.title: Political and Socio-Economic Conditions of Southern and Central States in Ethiopia
topics.description: Kingdoms of Enarya, Bizamo, Damot, Wolaita (Kawo), Kafa (Tato), Yem, Gamo, Hadiya, Dawuro, and Kambata.

topics.title: Population Movements, Expansion and Integration in Ethiopia
topics.description: Argobba, Afar, and Somali movements; the 16th-century Oromo population movement, causes, directions, and Barentu/Borana confederacies.

topics.title: Gadaa System of the Oromo
topics.description: Age-grades, 8-year democratic power transfer, Chaffe assembly, Abba Bokku, Abba Dula, Qallu institution, Siqqee women's rights, and Moggasa/Guddifacha integration.

topics.title: Moggasa and Guddifacha & Egalitarian Systems of Governance
topics.description: Social cohesion mechanisms and indigenous egalitarian governance systems (Sidama Luwa, Gedeo Baalle, Konso Xora, Burji, Nuer, Anuak).

book_chapters.title: Unit 7: States, Principalities, Population Movements & Interactions in Ethiopia 13th to Mid-16th C.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 8: Political, Social and Economic Processes in Ethiopia Mid-16th to Mid-19th C.
book_chapters.description: 8.1 Peoples and States of the Eastern, Central, Southern and Western Regions; 8.2 Gondarine Period (1636–1769); 8.3 The Zemene-Mesafint (1769–1855); 8.4 The Yejju Dynasty; 8.5 The Kingdom of Shewa

topics.title: Peoples and States of the Eastern, Central, Southern and Western Regions
topics.description: Emirate of Harar (Amir Nur, Jugol wall), Afar Sultanates (Awssa), Somali, Gurage, Silt'e, Hadiya, Kambata, Wolaita, Kafa, Gibe Oromo Monarchies (Jimma, Limmu-Enarya, Gumma, Gomma, Gera), Leqa-Naqamte, Leqa-Qellam, Sheikhdoms of Assosa/Bela Shangul/Khomosha, and Nilotic communities.

topics.title: Gondarine Period (1636–1769)
topics.description: Susenyos and Catholic interlude, Emperor Fasilides' Closed-Door Policy and founding of Gondar (1636), Fasil Ghebbi castles, Iyasu I, Empress Mentewab, urban commerce, and religious debates.

topics.title: The Zemene-Mesafint (1769–1855)
topics.description: Era of the Princes triggered by Ras Mikael Sehul (1769); regional warlordism, decline of imperial authority, devastation of peasantry, and Battle of Debre Abbay (1831).

topics.title: The Yejju Dynasty
topics.description: Ali Gwangul (Ali I), capital at Debre Tabor, Ras Gugsa Merso, and Yejju regency (Enderase) over the Gondarine puppet emperors.

topics.title: The Kingdom of Shewa
topics.description: Founded by Negasi Kristos in Menz; autonomous consolidation under Sahle Selassie (1813–1847), stability, trade, and foreign diplomacy.

book_chapters.title: Unit 8: Political, Social and Economic Processes in Ethiopia Mid-16th to Mid-19th C.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 9: The Age of Revolutions 1750s to 1815
book_chapters.description: 9.1 Industrial Capitalism in Europe; 9.2 The French Revolution (1789–1799); 9.3 The Napoleonic Era (1799–1815); 9.4 American War of Independence; 9.5 The Congress of Vienna (1814–1815)

topics.title: Industrial Capitalism in Europe
topics.description: Factory system, steam power, railway revolution, urbanization, rise of industrial bourgeoisie and proletariat working class.

topics.title: The French Revolution (1789–1799)
topics.description: Old Regime Three Estates, Enlightenment ideas (Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau), Storming of the Bastille (July 14, 1789), Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen, Jacobin Reign of Terror, and abolition of feudalism.

topics.title: The Napoleonic Era (1799–1815)
topics.description: Rise of Napoleon Bonaparte, Napoleonic Code, Continental System, spread of revolutionary reforms across Europe, Russian campaign (1812), and Battle of Waterloo (1815).

topics.title: American War of Independence
topics.description: Thirteen British colonies, "No taxation without representation," Stamp Act, Boston Tea Party, Declaration of Independence (July 4, 1776, Thomas Jefferson), George Washington, Treaty of Paris (1783), and US Constitution.

topics.title: The Congress of Vienna (1814–1815)
topics.description: Metternich, Castlereagh, Talleyrand; principles of Legitimacy, Balance of Power, and Compensation; redrawing the map of Europe.

book_chapters.title: Unit 9: The Age of Revolutions 1750s to 1815

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815–1914
book_chapters.description: 1.1 Features of Capitalism; 1.2 Features of Nationalism and Formation of Nation States; 1.3 Unification of Italy; 1.4 Unification of Germany; 1.5 The American Civil War (1861–1865); 1.6 Nationalism and the "Eastern Question"

topics.title: Features of Capitalism
topics.description: Private ownership of means of production, free market competition, profit motive, wage labor, and Second Industrial Revolution (steel, electricity, chemicals, petroleum).

topics.title: Features of Nationalism and Formation of Nation States
topics.description: Factors promoting 19th-century nationalism: shared language, history, culture, territory, and reaction against Napoleonic/dynastic rule.

topics.title: Unification of Italy
topics.description: Risorgimento leaders: Giuseppe Mazzini (Young Italy), Count Camillo di Cavour (Piedmont-Sardinia diplomacy), Giuseppe Garibaldi (Red Shirts), and King Victor Emmanuel II (1861–1870).

topics.title: Unification of Germany
topics.description: Zollverein customs union, Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Danish War (1864), Austro-Prussian War (1866), and Franco-Prussian War (1870–71).

topics.title: The American Civil War (1861–1865)
topics.description: Conflict between industrial North (Union) and plantation slave-owning South (Confederacy); Abraham Lincoln, Homestead Act, Emancipation Proclamation (1863), and 13th/14th/15th Amendments.

topics.title: Nationalism and the "Eastern Question"
topics.description: Decline of the Ottoman Empire ("Sick Man of Europe"), Balkan nationalist uprisings (Greece, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania), Crimean War, and Balkan Wars (1912–1913).

book_chapters.title: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815–1914

book_chapters.description: 2.1 General Background to Colonialism; 2.2 The Motives of European Colonialism; 2.3 Scramble for Africa and the Berlin Conference (1884–1885); 2.4 Colonial Policies and Administration; 2.5 Early African Resistance Movements Against Colonialism; 2.6 Impacts of Colonial Rule on Africa

topics.title: General Background to Colonialism
topics.description: Transition from "legitimate trade" and coastal outposts to full-scale imperial partition of Africa.

topics.title: The Motives of European Colonialism
topics.description: Economic demand for raw materials, captive markets, investment outlets, strategic waterways (Suez Canal), and "Civilizing Mission" ideology.

topics.title: Scramble for Africa and the Berlin Conference (1884–1885)
topics.description: King Leopold II in Congo, Anglo-French rivalry, Otto von Bismarck, and the Berlin Conference "Principle of Effective Occupation".

topics.title: Colonial Policies and Administration
topics.description: Company Rule, British Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), French Direct Rule (Assimilation and Association), Settler Rule, and Divide-and-Rule.

topics.title: Early African Resistance Movements Against Colonialism
topics.description: Samori Toure (Mandinka Empire), Ashanti resistance (Yaa Asantewaa), Maji-Maji Rebellion (Tanganyika), Urabi Pasha (Egypt), Mahdist Sudan, and Herero-Nama uprising.

topics.title: Impacts of Colonial Rule on Africa
topics.description: Arbitrary borders, loss of sovereignty, monocrop cash-crop dependency, land alienation, and infrastructure built solely for resource extraction.

book_chapters.title: Unit 2: Africa & the Colonial Experience (1880s–1960s)

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 3: Social, Economic & Political Developments in Ethiopia Mid-19th C. to 1941
book_chapters.description: 3.1 Long Distance Trade & Cottage Industry in Ethiopia in the 19th Century; 3.2 The Making of the Modern Ethiopian State 1855–1913; 3.3 External Aggressions and the Struggle for the Defense of National Sovereignty, 1871–1896; 3.4 Inception of Power Struggle Among the Ruling Elites, 1906–1935; 3.5 Fascist Italian Aggression and Patriotic Resistance (1935–1941)

topics.title: Long Distance Trade & Cottage Industry in Ethiopia in the 19th Century
topics.description: Jabarti and Afqala merchants, trade routes linking Bonga/Jimma to Massawa, Zeila, Berbera, and Metemma; Maria Theresa Thaler and amole salt bars; cottage crafts (smithing, weaving, pottery, tanning).

topics.title: The Making of the Modern Ethiopian State 1855–1913
topics.description: Emperor Tewodros II (ending Zemene-Mesafint, Gafat Sebastopol, Maqdala 1868), Tekle Giyorgis II, Yohannes IV (Liche Agreement 1878, Boru Meda Council), and Menelik II (territorial incorporation, founding of Addis Ababa 1886, modernization, 1907 Ministerial Cabinet).

topics.title: External Aggressions and the Struggle for the Defense of National Sovereignty, 1871–1896
topics.description: Egyptian invasions defeated at Gundet (1875) and Gura (1876); Hewett (Adwa) Treaty (1884); Mahdist battles (Kufit, Metemma 1889); Italian encroachment, Dogali (1887), Treaty of Wuchale (Article XVII), and the historic Victory of Adwa (March 1, 1896).

topics.title: Inception of Power Struggle Among the Ruling Elites, 1906–1935
topics.description: Empress Taytu Bitul, Lij Iyasu's reforms, 1916 coup and Battle of Segele, Dual Rule (Diarchy) of Empress Zewditu and Regent Ras Tafari Makonnen, and coronation of Emperor Haile Selassie I (1930) & 1931 Constitution.

topics.title: Fascist Italian Aggression and Patriotic Resistance (1935–1941)
topics.description: Walwal Incident (1934), Northern and Southern Fronts (Amba Aradom, Tembien, Maychew, Qorahe, Genale Dorya), Italian East Africa (AOI), Graziani Massacre (Yekatit 12, 1937), Black Lions, Abune Petros, Patriots (Arbegnoch) & Women Patriots, and 1941 Liberation Campaign (Gideon Force).

book_chapters.title: Unit 3: Social, Economic & Political Developments in Ethiopia Mid-19th C. to 1941

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
book_chapters.description: 4.1 The First World War: Causes, Course and the Consequence (1914–1918); 4.2 The October 1917 Russian Revolution: Cause, Course and Results; 4.3 The League of Nations & the Worldwide Economic Crisis; 4.4 The Rise of Fascism in Italy, Nazism in Germany and Militarism in Japan; 4.5 The Second World War: 1939–45

topics.title: The First World War: Causes, Course and the Consequence (1914–1918)
topics.description: MAIN causes (Militarism, Alliances: Triple Entente vs Triple Alliance, Imperialism, Nationalism), Sarajevo assassination, Western/Eastern fronts, US entry, and Treaty of Versailles (1919).

topics.title: The October 1917 Russian Revolution: Cause, Course and Results
topics.description: Tsarist autocracy, 1905 Revolution, February 1917 Revolution, Vladimir Lenin and the Bolsheviks ("Peace, Land, and Bread"), October Revolution, Civil War (Reds vs Whites), NEP, and Stalin's Five-Year Plans.

topics.title: The League of Nations & the Worldwide Economic Crisis
topics.description: Structure and weaknesses of the League of Nations; the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the Great Depression.

topics.title: The Rise of Fascism in Italy, Nazism in Germany and Militarism in Japan
topics.description: Benito Mussolini's March on Rome (1922), Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime (1933), and Japanese militarist expansion into Manchuria (1931) and China (1937).

topics.title: The Second World War: 1939–45
